findings.summary: In one sample the skillet sprite is a filled disc with a 1-unit straight handle. At 1x in the grid it reads as a magnifying glass or a lollipop rather than a pan. The Imagery rule asks for solid defining parts at least 2 units thick, and the handle is thinner than that. The other two samples draw a 2-unit handle and read as a pan. The reference's small props stay legible at the same scale (reference p2-i2.png).

On every blog route of one sample, the one-line footer note sits to the right of the newsletter window, on the window's bottom edge, at about x 640–1130. It reads as a stray caption attached to the form. The other two samples put it on its own line under the window. In the reference the footer line sits below its own rule (reference p1-desktop-light.png).

In one sample the cart line item is a bare row on the page background: no subtle card, no hue bar and no category label. The other two samples, and the rest of that sample's store, show items as subtle cards with a hue top bar. Next to the framed totals and checkout windows, the item reads as unstyled.

notes: SCOPE (confirm step, 3 samples). Samples are 20261018-120446-s2, 20261018-120446-s1 and 20261018-112309 for blog, commerce, dashboard and settings, plus the docs and landing holdouts (s1). Every gate passes in every sample (eval-2.md). Palette consistency is 0.917, 0.938 and 0.938; type consistency is 1. The harness measured no layout defects, so there was nothing to confirm or dismiss. Not penalized, as known harness capture gaps: the sticky header captured mid-page in full-page state shots (commerce state-checkout-errors, dashboard state-empty-filter, blog state-search-empty, settings state-profile-errors) and the dialog scrim ending at about 900px (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png). Light and dark captures are identical because the system is dark only.

RC.8 MAJORS, checked across all three samples. (1) Garment sleeves: FIXED in 3 of 3. Every sweater and coat is one silhouette, with sleeves joined fill against fill and angled out to the cuffs (commerce s1 drawings/products-merino-crew-sweater-d2.png, s2 drawings/products-merino-crew-sweater-d2.png, and both home grids). No straight bars hang beside a body. In each sample the sweater, coat and tee differ in outline. (2) Item-card summaries clamped at 2 lines: FIXED in 3 of 3. All product summaries are whole in up to 3 lines at 1440 (commerce s1 and s2 home-desktop-light.png), and blog .cards show whole summaries of up to 4 lines.

RC.9 SCREEN MINORS (critic-1), not re-raised. Several now recur, listed so the lead can decide: (a) the chart plot past `size.chart`, now 2 of 3 (dashboard s1 home-desktop-light.png, plot about 410px; its agent-report.md gives the same reason: the panels had to level and the 5 activity items could not be trimmed). s2 solved it with a Total/Peak/Average row under a plot of about 240px. The spec's panel-levelling rule still offers no third option. (b) A tote drawn as one squared arch over a box, reading close to a padlock at detail size: 2 of 3 (commerce s1 products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-light.png). s2 draws two separate loops. (c) The hero's near-ground outline with square notches: 3 of 3. Carried rc.8 minors also still recur: the key ring and tea towels fail the name test (s1's towels read as two shopping bags), empty-state titles are body size, the user menu opens with no option highlighted (dashboard s2), and the password form leaves a band about 500px empty (settings s2). None is worse than published.

UPDATE GOAL (1.2.0, leftovers from the 1.1.0 review): REACHED in all three samples. Hero leads carry real signs and defining features: a NEWS press house with a sawtooth roof, rollers and a chimney (blog s2 drawings/home-d1.png), and an INK works with a chimney, gear plate and delivery truck (blog s1 drawings/home-d1.png). Mobile hero: the lead shows under a band of sky (blog s2 home-mobile-light.png; in s1 the lead is whole and only the side truck is cut). Detail sprites fill about 48–49% of the window (commerce s2 products-merino-crew-sweater-desktop-light.png, s1 products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-light.png). Sleeves are attached. Every newsletter has a 'Subscribe to the newsletter' h2. The store name is whole on mobile. The hill has a teal rim and a diagonal stepped path. Mobile tables show Project and Status only (dashboard s1 and s2 home-mobile-light.png).

COMPARED WITH PUBLISHED 1.1.0: nothing worse in any sample. The hero leads, garments, product-page sprite size, banners per item (commerce s2: KNIT; s1: TOTE; each sample's agent-report lists 11 distinct product buildings), varied blog banner leads (TYPE, POST, EDIT; each about 105–115px tall), the mobile table and the store name are all better or equal.

SIGNATURE (4). Present in all four apps of every sample and placed as Applying the concept says: a full-bleed hero, banners on articles, about and product detail, strips on catalogue, cart, dashboard and settings, inline figures, framed vignettes in empty states, and the checkered ground strip on every screen. Motion is stepped: nc-drift runs at 120000ms with steps(40) (blog s2 motion/motion-m1.png, landing s1 motion/motion-m1.png). Not a 5: strip props are still 20–50px and simpler than the reference's trees and figure at the same scale (dashboard s2 home-desktop-light.png vs reference p2-i2.png), and some sprites carry the name-test minors above. The moon is a dithered halo disc on every scene. That is the spec's own `moon()` recipe and the reference also has a haloed moon (p1-i1.png), so it is not raised.

HOLDOUTS. Docs and landing carry the system with no blocker or major. Each has its own lead with a real sign word (YARD; a clock tower and an hourglass house), a framed hero Window with a gold commit, hue-bar card grids, a sidebar with the marker and the ground strip (docs home-desktop-light.png, docs-guides-configuration-desktop-light.png, landing home-desktop-light.png, pricing-desktop-light.png). Search results open in a framed window under a gold-focused field (docs state-search-results-desktop-light.png). The mobile menu is a titled window with marker items (docs state-mobile-nav-open-mobile-light.png).

OTHER SCORES. Reference fidelity (4): night ground, cream pixel type, 4px windows, dither rules under h2s, one gold commit with a hard shadow, the gold ▶ marker, hue top bars and square bullets, block meters and the grass strip, as in reference p1-desktop-light.png, without copying the cabin, figure or snow. Cross-app consistency (4): one family across apps and samples. Dashboard s1 puts its navigation in the header rather than a sidebar, which the Layout shells allow, so it is not a defect. Hierarchy (4): scene and h1 first, 48px KPIs, 48px prices with a gold Add to cart; the carried empty-state title size is the weak point. Spacing (4): the 4px scale holds, panels end level and controls sharing a row share one height (blog email + Subscribe, settings Save + Reset, dashboard search + Search). Component states (4): card hover shows the marker and a lighter card (commerce s1 state-card-hover-desktop-dark.png). Invalid fields get a gold focus frame on the first one, danger frames and '!' messages (commerce s1 and s2 state-checkout-errors-desktop-dark.png, settings s2 state-profile-errors-desktop-dark.png). The plan change opens a titled window dialog with a framed close button, Cancel and a gold Confirm (settings s1 state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png). Loading shows skeleton KPI tiles and a disabled 'Refreshing ...' button (dashboard s1 state-loading-desktop-dark.png). Empty results show a vignette, an empty meter and a framed ▶ Clear filters. Polish (4): radius 0, 2/4px borders, no browser defaults left over.

VERDICT INPUT. No blocker and no major in any of the three samples or the holdouts. Both rc.8 majors stay fixed across all samples, the 1.2.0 update goal is reached, and nothing is worse than published 1.1.0. Three new minors, each in 1 of 3, are listed once. The confirm step passes.
